mutants.why: The tightened RFC 4155 shape (clock time + 4-digit year) is what keeps prose beginning 'From ' from splitting a message. Weakening it to '^From \S+' makes the body line 'From now on we meet on Tuesdays.' match and be indexed as a second separator. fromPrefixedBodyLineIsNotASeparator asserts QCOMPARE(parser.messageCount(), 1).

The guard rejects a malformed 'From  ' (double-space, empty sender). Inverting == to != rejects EVERY real 'From ' separator (whose sender's first char is not a space), so isFromLine returns false, open() calls it an invalid MBOX, and indexing finds zero messages. indexSingleMessage asserts QVERIFY(parser.isOpen()) and QCOMPARE(parser.messageCount(), 2).

A message's raw slice runs from its own offset to the NEXT message's offset. Dropping the +1 makes end==start for every non-last message, so message_size<=0 -> read_error and message 0 is skipped, leaving only the last message. readMessagesSync asserts QCOMPARE(result->size(), 2) and result->at(0).subject == "Hello World".

This branch enters single-part handling only when the message is NOT multipart/*. Corrupting the 'multipart/' literal to 'multipartX/' makes the check never recognize a real multipart message, so multipart/mixed wrongly enters the single-part path where is_non_text is true and the whole body is misfiled as one attachment instead of being split into parts. nestedMultipartRecoversBodyAndAttachment asserts detail->body_plain.contains("Hello plain body").

A MIME boundary delimiter line is '--<boundary>' (RFC 2046). Building it with a single dash ('-B') never prefix-matches the real '--B' lines, so isBoundaryDelimiterLine never fires and the body never splits into parts. multipartWithManyPartsSplitsCorrectly asserts QCOMPARE(detail->attachments.size(), 3).

After stripping the boundary prefix, only an empty remainder (opening) or exactly '--' (closing) is a real delimiter line. Flipping == to != makes any prefix-sharing body line (rest != '--') count as a boundary AND breaks real closing lines (rest == '--' now yields false), so a shared-prefix line is consumed as a delimiter and vanishes from the body. boundaryPrefixLineNotTreatedAsBoundary asserts detail->body_plain.contains("--ABCDEF is not a boundary.").

An OPENING delimiter ('--B', no trailing '--') starts a part so in_part must become true; a CLOSING delimiter ('--B--') ends it. Dropping the ! sets in_part=false after every opening delimiter, so subsequent part content is never accumulated and all parts are lost. nestedMultipartRecoversBodyAndAttachment asserts detail->body_plain.contains("Hello plain body").

At a boundary, a populated in-progress part must be emitted. Requiring current to be EMPTY instead means a non-empty part is never flushed nor reset, so every part merges into one buffer and only a single text part is produced -- zero attachments. multipartWithManyPartsSplitsCorrectly asserts QCOMPARE(detail->attachments.size(), 3).

A sub-part that is itself multipart/* must be recursed into. Breaking the literal ('multipartX/') so it never matches stops recursion, so the parts inside an inner multipart/related (the inline pic.png) are never enumerated. readAttachmentDataAlignsWithRecursiveEnumeration asserts QCOMPARE(detail->attachments.size(), 2) with attachments.at(0).long_filename == "pic.png".

A leaf part is recovered as an attachment when it is non-text (or has an attachment disposition). Dropping the ! flips the decision so only text/* parts are 'non_text', so an image/png inline part with no attachment disposition is dropped instead of recovered. readAttachmentDataAlignsWithRecursiveEnumeration asserts detail->attachments.at(0).long_filename == "pic.png" (the image/png inline part) and attachments.size() == 2.

This trailing flush recovers the final part of a multipart body that has NO closing '--B--' delimiter (current_part still holds it). trailingPartRecoveredWhenClosingDelimiterMissing builds a multipart/mixed whose stream ends right after the final attachment part with the closing '--B--' omitted, so consumeMimeLine never flushed the last part and only this end-of-body flush recovers it; the test asserts QCOMPARE(detail->attachments.size(), 1) with long_filename 'tail.bin' (and readAttachmentData(0,0) yields its bytes). Inverting !current_part.isEmpty() to current_part.isEmpty() skips the flush, the truncated final part is dropped, attachments.size() becomes 0, and the assertion fails.
